summary:
VitalOrbit is a health monitoring system for astronauts on long-duration missions beyond low Earth orbit (lunar base, Gateway, Mars transit). It turns raw health indicators into clear guidance the crew can act on, even when Earth is hours away.

A 10-second telemetry feed (heart rate, SpO₂, respiratory rate, skin temperature, activity), manual measurements and cabin data (CO₂, radiation) trigger rule-based, explainable alerts: hypoxia, high CO₂, sleep loss, fever, sensor failure. Each alert opens a step-by-step protocol with looping pictogram clips until the crew confirms each step. VitalOrbit never diagnoses or prescribes: it detects, guides first response and proposes human review.

Data is stored in Zabbix 8.0 (Docker, PostgreSQL). Each sample carries valid, quality and observed_at, so data state is separate from clinical result: a missing signal is never shown as “all good”. Alerts close only with new valid data. Observations can be translated to HL7 FHIR R4.

A voluntary “refuge” tab (NASA Cognition-style game, diary, playlist) lets the crew rest and gives the ground team a non-invasive mood signal.

Tools: Zabbix, Docker, PostgreSQL, FastAPI, Next.js, FHIR R4, ffmpeg.

Limitations: all data is simulated; thresholds and protocols are demonstrative, not clinically validated.
details:
WHAT IT DOES
VitalOrbit helps astronauts assess their own health on missions beyond low Earth orbit, following NASA’s Human Research Program hazards (radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, gravity fields, hostile closed environments). The mission model is hybrid: the spacecraft works autonomously and sends reports to the ground when a link is available. The whole crew sees physiological data; mood, stress and cohesion are private (the crew sees only a color, the ground psychologist sees the value).

HOW IT WORKS

  • Data layer: Zabbix 8.0 (Docker, PostgreSQL) collects data from astronaut hosts via Zabbix Agent 2 every 10 s. Each sample carries valid, quality and observed_at, so the system separates data state (fresh, stale, no data, not interpretable) from clinical result (normal, watch, alert). A missing signal is never shown as “all good”.
  • Alerts: Zabbix triggers are the single source of truth, delivered by webhook. An alert is closed only with new valid data, never by acknowledgement alone.
  • Interoperability: observations can be translated on the fly to HL7 FHIR R4 with LOINC codes and UCUM units.
  • Protocols: eight demonstration protocols (hypoxia, high CO₂, sleep loss, solar storm, deconditioning, fever, orthostatic hypotension, sensor failure). Each has one action per step, roles (affected, companion, commander) and escalation rules. Pictogram videos (29 s, with audio) are split into per-step clips and played by a React/Next.js step player that loops each clip until the crew member confirms.
  • Behavioral health refuge: a voluntary tab with games from NASA’s Cognition battery, a diary and a “what song would you like to hear?” playlist. It lets the crew rest and gives the ground team a non-invasive signal of mood changes. Zabbix only stores this data; assessment is done by the ground team.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT
It guides first response when no doctor is aboard, supports crew self-assessment and gives flight surgeons structured, interoperable data, even when Earth is hours away. Our principle: first the person, then the data. VitalOrbit never diagnoses or prescribes: it detects, guides and proposes human review.

TOOLS
Zabbix 8.0, Docker, PostgreSQL, FastAPI, Next.js/React/Tailwind, HL7 FHIR R4, Python (Pillow) and ffmpeg for video, Inter font.

CREATIVITY
A refuge that disguises psychological screening as voluntary leisure, and a data-quality-first alert model that never confuses “no data” with “healthy”.

LIMITATIONS (TRANSPARENT)
All data is simulated. Thresholds and protocols are for demonstration, based on public sources, and are not clinically validated.
